label: GO after an unrewarded trial, agent strongly committed to a2
explanation: Fires only at the GO step (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward==0; essentially never after reward), and only when the model is about to choose a2 with a strongly negative policy logit (choice < ~-8.9; sharp threshold, -8 or -10 do worse). Typical history: a2 then rare transition to S1 and no reward (model-based stay on a2), the observed-history-only predicate GO & prev_reward==0 & prev_action==2 & prev_state==1 gets P 0.97 R 0.76 F1 0.85 on dev; the extra recall from the choice threshold comes from first-trial-in-window GO steps (previous trial outside the window) and weaker activations after common-unrewarded a2 trials where the agent still strongly prefers a2. Does not fire for a1 choices, after rewarded trials, or for weak a2 preferences. choice is the agent own GO policy, so no future variable is used. Activation coverage rises with activation quartile (0.81 to 0.94), consistent with larger activations at more extreme a2 preference.

issues: Several basic claims hold. The feature fires only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps). It almost never fires after a reward (GO & prev_reward==1 gives recall 0.007). The recorded predicate scores test P 0.973, R 0.854, F1 0.910.

The claim that the choice threshold catches 'weaker activations after common-unrewarded a2 trials' is essentially false. On test, GO & prev_reward==0 & prev_action==2 & prev_common==1 & choice<-8.91 has recall 0.004 (precision 0.39), and the same history with choice>=-8.91 has precision 0.0005. Nearly all the extra recall from the choice term comes from window-first GO steps (rel==-3, where prev_action is -1 because the previous trial is outside the window): rel==-3 & prev_reward==0 & choice<-8.91 gives P 0.977, R 0.161. So the choice threshold mostly stands in for history that is missing from the window.

The label overclaims or misplaces the cause. The feature is driven by the observed history 'last trial was a2, then a rare transition (to S1), then no reward' (prev_common==0 carries 78% of the activation mass; prev_common==1 carries 3%), not by how strongly the agent is committed to a2. The threshold also drops real cases: rare-unrewarded a2 trials with choice>=-8.91 have precision 0.82 but are excluded (about 5.7% of test recall).

Systematic miss class: switching to a2 after an unrewarded common a1 trial (prev_action==1, prev_common==1, action==2). It gives weak activations, test precision 0.26 and recall 0.055, and neither predicate covers it. This is a minor secondary class.
A predicate using only observed history, with a fallback to the choice threshold only on the window-first trial, beats the recorded predicate on test: P 0.968, R 0.907, F1 0.937, mass recall 0.937.
skeptic.revised_label: GO after an a2 choice that had a rare transition and went unrewarded (the model-based 'stay on a2' case); on the window's first trial, where that history is outside the window, it shows up as a strong a2 preference
